jp: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]を干[ほ]そうとしたら、雨[あめ]が{ざあざあ|on-weather}降[ふ]り出[だ]して、母[はは]が慌[あわ]てて取[と]り込[こ]んだ。
en: Just as we were about to hang out the laundry, the rain started pouring, and Mom hurriedly took it in.
why: Heavy rain is ざあざあ; しとしと is a soft drizzle and the others are wind and shine.

jp: 朝[あさ]から雨[あめ]が{しとしと|on-weather}降[ふ]っていて、祖母[そぼ]は縁側[えんがわ]でお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]んでいる。
en: Rain has been falling softly since morning, and Grandmother is drinking tea on the veranda.
why: Quiet, steady drizzle is しとしと; ざあざあ would be a downpour.

jp: 買[か]い物[もの]の帰[かえ]り道[みち]、雨[あめ]が{ぽつぽつ|on-weather}落[お]ちてきたので、家[いえ]まで走[はし]った。
en: On the way home from shopping, raindrops began to fall here and there, so I ran the rest of the way.
why: The first scattered drops are ぽつぽつ; ざあざあ is a downpour and ごろごろ is thunder.

jp: 夜[よる]、強[つよ]い風[かぜ]が{びゅうびゅう|on-weather}吹[ふ]いて、家[いえ]じゅうの窓[まど]が揺[ゆ]れていた。
en: At night a strong wind howled, and the windows all over the house were shaking.
why: A strong whistling wind is びゅうびゅう; the others describe shine or rain.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]、父[ちち]が車[くるま]を洗[あら]って、{ぴかぴか|on-weather}にした。
en: On Sunday my father washed the car until it was shiny and clean.
why: A clean, polished surface is ぴかぴか; the other words are rain, thunder and wind.

jp: 弟[おとうと]の目[め]は、新[あたら]しいおもちゃを見[み]て{きらきら|on-weather}輝[かがや]いていた。
en: My little brother's eyes sparkled when he saw the new toy.
why: Twinkling, sparkling light is きらきら; the other words are rain and thunder.

jp: 夕方[ゆうがた]、遠[とお]くで雷[かみなり]が{ごろごろ|on-weather}鳴[な]り始[はじ]めたので、母[はは]は窓[まど]を閉[し]めた。
en: In the evening thunder began to rumble in the distance, so Mother closed the window.
why: Rumbling thunder is ごろごろ; the others are rain, sparkle and wind.
